common_name: Molten Lava Plant (Fire Fern, Volcanic Shamrock)

planting.note: Set out divisions or rooted cuttings after all frost danger has passed in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade; this Costa Rican species forms a low, spreading mat from creeping, slightly succulent stems rather than from bulbous rhizomes like Oxalis triangularis.

directions: Grow in partial shade with moist, well-drained soil, siting plants where they get bright filtered light rather than harsh midday sun, which can scorch the thin foliage. Molten Lava produces small, clover-like leaflets in glowing bronze, copper, or lime-green depending on cultivar and light exposure, forming a dense, low groundcover or trailing container plant quite different in habit from the taller, bulb-forming Oxalis triangularis. Small five-petaled yellow flowers appear sporadically above the foliage through the warm months but are secondary to the colorful foliage display. In zone 9 and warmer it persists outdoors as a perennial groundcover or edging plant; elsewhere bring indoors as a houseplant or treat as a warm-season annual, since it has no tolerance for frost.
